Levi's Stadium in August 2014 during a 49ers game.

Levi's Stadium is designed as an open stadium with a natural grass field. It has a seating capacity of 68,500, expandable to approximately 75,000 to host major events like the [Super Bowl](/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl"), [WrestleMania](/wiki/WrestleMania "WrestleMania"), and the [FIFA World Cup](/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"). On June 27, 2015, The Grateful Dead Fare Thee Well Tour made history by extending the stadium seating capacity to 83,000, although only 77,000 attended the event over two nights. To date, the record attendance for a single day event was almost 80,000 for an [Ed Sheeran](/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") concert on September 16, 2023.[[22]](#cite_note-22)

The seating design of the stadium places approximately two-thirds of the fans in the lower bowl, which is one of the largest of its kind in the entire NFL. The design features significantly improved accessibility and seating options for fans with special needs and disabilities when compared to the 49ers former home, the now-demolished Candlestick Park. The configuration is similar to [Ford Field](/wiki/Ford_Field "Ford Field"), home of the NFL's [Detroit Lions](/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions"), with the majority of the [luxury suites](/wiki/Luxury_box "Luxury box") on one side of the field, which puts the fans in the upper deck closer to the action.

As a multi-use facility, the stadium can be configured for special touring events including concerts, motocross events, indoor/outdoor conferences, and other community events. This list includes athletes who have won **six or more** Olympic medals over their sporting career. Medals won in the [1906 Intercalated Games](/wiki/1906_Intercalated_Games "1906 Intercalated Games") are not included.
For simplicity, when an athlete has won medals for more than one nation, their entry in this list only mentions the last **Nation** represented. The **Years** listed for each athlete only include the Games in which they won medals. More detailed information is provided in the linked articles for the individual athletes.

In cases where two or more athletes have the same number of total medals, the first tiebreaker is the number of gold medals, followed by the number of silver medals. If the tied athletes have exactly the same number of gold, silver and bronze medals, the ranking is given as a tie and the athletes are listed in order first by career years and then alphabetically by surname.

Tokyo :: Geography :: chunk_0017
The mainland portion of Tokyo lies northwest of [Tokyo Bay](/wiki/Tokyo_Bay "Tokyo Bay") and measures about 90 km (56 mi) east to west and 25 km (16 mi) north to south. The average elevation in Tokyo is 40 m (131 ft).[[100]](#cite_note-102) [Chiba Prefecture](/wiki/Chiba_Prefecture "Chiba Prefecture") borders it to the east, [Yamanashi](/wiki/Yamanashi_Prefecture "Yamanashi Prefecture") to the west, [Kanagawa](/wiki/Kanagawa_Prefecture "Kanagawa Prefecture") to the south, and [Saitama](/wiki/Saitama_Prefecture "Saitama Prefecture") to the north. Mainland Tokyo is further subdivided into the special wards (occupying the eastern half) and the Tama area (多摩地域) stretching westwards. Tokyo has a [latitude](/wiki/Latitude "Latitude") of 35.65 (near the [36th parallel north](/wiki/36th_parallel_north "36th parallel north")), which makes it more southern than [Rome](/wiki/Rome "Rome") (41.90), [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") (40.71) and [Beijing](/wiki/Beijing "Beijing") (39.91).[[101]](#cite_note-103)

Within the administrative boundaries of Tokyo Metropolis are two island chains in the Pacific Ocean directly south: the [Izu Islands](/wiki/Izu_Islands "Izu Islands"), and the [Ogasawara Islands](/wiki/Ogasawara_Islands "Ogasawara Islands"), which stretch more than 1,000 km (620 mi) away from the mainland. Because of these islands and the mountainous regions to the west, Tokyo's overall population density figures far under-represent the real figures for the urban and suburban regions of Tokyo.[[102]](#cite_note-104)

The Soviet Union performed the first hard Moon landing, in which the spacecraft intentionally crashed into the Moon at high speed, with the [Luna 2](/wiki/Luna_2 "Luna 2") spacecraft in 1959, a feat the U.S. duplicated in 1962 with [Ranger 4](/wiki/Ranger_4 "Ranger 4").

The [2018 meeting in Charlevoix, Canada](/wiki/44th_G7_summit "44th G7 summit"), was marred by fractious negotiations concerning tariffs and Donald Trump's position that Russia should be reinstated to the G7. The Trump administration had just imposed steel and aluminium tariffs on many countries, including European countries that are fellow members of the G7, and Canada, the host country for the 2018 meeting. Trump expressed dismay at Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau for holding a press conference in which Canada restated its position on tariffs (a public criticism of Trump's economic policy), and directed his representatives at the meeting not to sign the economic section of the joint communiqué that is typically issued at the conclusion of the meeting.
German Chancellor Angela Merkel described Trump's behaviour as a "depressing withdrawal", while French President Emmanuel Macron invited him "to be serious".[[82]](#cite_note-82) In the final statement signed by all members except the US, the G7 announced its intention to recall sanctions and to be ready to take further restrictive measures within the next months against the Russian Federation for its failure to completely implement the [Minsk Agreement](/wiki/Minsk_Agreement "Minsk Agreement").[[83]](#cite_note-auto-83)

In 1779, not trusting then provost [William Smith](/wiki/William_Smith_(Episcopalian_priest) "William Smith (Episcopalian priest)")'s [Loyalist](/wiki/Loyalist_(American_Revolution) "Loyalist (American Revolution)") tendencies, the revolutionary State Legislature created a university, and in 1785 the legislature changed name to [University of the State of Pennsylvania](/wiki/University_of_the_State_of_Pennsylvania "University of the State of Pennsylvania").[[49]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-56)[[h]](#cite_note-57) The result was a schism, with Smith continuing to operate an attenuated version of the College of Philadelphia. Main article: [Census in China](/wiki/Census_in_China "Census in China")

The People's Republic of China conducted censuses in [1953](/wiki/1953_Chinese_census "1953 Chinese census"), [1964](/wiki/1964_Chinese_census "1964 Chinese census"), [1982](/wiki/1982_Chinese_census "1982 Chinese census"), [1990](/wiki/1990_Chinese_census "1990 Chinese census"), [2000](/wiki/2000_Chinese_census "2000 Chinese census"), [2010](/wiki/2010_Chinese_census "2010 Chinese census"), and [2020](/wiki/2020_Chinese_census "2020 Chinese census"). In 1987, the government announced that the fourth national census would take place in 1990 and that there would be one every ten years thereafter. The 1982 census (which reported a total population of 1,008,180,738) is generally accepted as significantly more reliable, accurate, and thorough than the previous two.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Various international organizations eagerly assisted the Chinese in conducting the 1982 census, including the [United Nations Fund for Population Activities](/wiki/United_Nations_Fund_for_Population_Activities "United Nations Fund for Population Activities"), which donated US$100.0 million between 1980 and 1989 for a variety of projects, one of which being the 1982 census.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

China was the world's most populous nation until being surpassed by India in 2023.[[22]](#cite_note-22)

By the seventh census in 2020, the total population had reached to 1,419,933,142, with the mainland having 1,411,778,724, Hong Kong having 7,474,200, and Macau having 683,218. However, this number is disputed by [obstetrics](/wiki/Obstetrics "Obstetrics") researcher [Yi Fuxian](/wiki/Yi_Fuxian "Yi Fuxian"), who argues that data related to population growth is inflated by local governments to obtain financial subsidies from the central government.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

Eastern Front (World War II) :: part 08 :: chunk_0007
The two principal belligerent powers in the Eastern Front were Germany and the Soviet Union, along with their respective allies. Though they never sent ground troops to the Eastern Front, the [United States](/wiki/Military_history_of_the_United_States_during_World_War_II "Military history of the United States during World War II") and the [United Kingdom](/wiki/Military_history_of_the_United_Kingdom_during_World_War_II "Military history of the United Kingdom during World War II") both provided substantial material aid to the Soviet Union in the form of the [Lend-Lease](/wiki/Lend-Lease "Lend-Lease") program, along with naval and air support.

The joint [German–Finnish operations](/wiki/Operation_Silver_Fox "Operation Silver Fox") across the northernmost Finnish–Soviet border and in the [Murmansk region](/wiki/Murmansk_Oblast "Murmansk Oblast") are considered part of the Eastern Front. In addition, the Soviet–Finnish [Continuation War](/wiki/Continuation_War "Continuation War") is generally also considered the northern flank of the Eastern Front.
